laws.title: Illegal Firearms Possession
laws.subtitle: Owning unregistered or prohibited weapons
laws.fullDescription: Guatemalan law requires all firearms to be registered with the National Registry of Arms and Munitions (RENAM). Possessing unregistered weapons, military-grade arms, or modified firearms is a serious criminal offense in a country deeply affected by gun violence.
laws.penalty: 5 to 13 years imprisonment
exceptions: Licensed security companies
Military and police forces
Sport shooters with valid permits

quiz.q: Which body registers civilian firearms in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: RENAM (National Registry of Arms and Munitions) is responsible for registering all civilian firearms in Guatemala.

laws.title: Drug Trafficking
laws.subtitle: Transporting or distributing narcotics
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala is a major transit country for cocaine moving from South America to the United States. Drug trafficking is treated as a serious crime with severe penalties. Organized criminal networks including MS-13 and Barrio 18 are deeply involved in the trade.
laws.penalty: 12 to 20 years imprisonment
exceptions: Licensed pharmaceutical distribution

quiz.q: What role does Guatemala play in regional drug trafficking?
quiz.explanation: Guatemala is primarily a transit country for cocaine moving from South American producers toward North American markets.

laws.title: Human Trafficking
laws.subtitle: Exploiting people for labor or sexual purposes
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala has significant human trafficking problems, both internally and as a transit and source country. The law criminalizes all forms of trafficking including forced labor, sexual exploitation, and child trafficking. Victims are often indigenous communities and women.
laws.penalty: 8 to 18 years imprisonment; up to 20 for aggravated cases
exceptions: None — all trafficking is criminal
laws.sourceLabel: Guatemala Law Against Sexual Violence, Exploitation and Trafficking

quiz.q: Which communities are particularly vulnerable to trafficking in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Indigenous communities and women in Guatemala face heightened vulnerability to human trafficking due to socioeconomic marginalization.

laws.title: Corruption and Bribery
laws.subtitle: Offering or accepting bribes in public office
laws.fullDescription: Corruption is a serious problem in Guatemala, leading to major prosecutorial efforts including the internationally-backed CICIG anti-corruption commission. Both offering and accepting bribes by public officials is criminalized under Guatemalan law.
laws.penalty: 5 to 10 years imprisonment; removal from office
exceptions: None — bribery of officials is always criminal

quiz.q: What international body assisted Guatemala with anti-corruption prosecutions?
quiz.explanation: CICIG (International Commission Against Impunity in Guatemala) was a UN-backed body that supported major anti-corruption prosecutions.

laws.title: Illegal Deforestation
laws.subtitle: Cutting protected forests without authorization
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala has experienced significant deforestation, particularly in the Petén region which contains part of the Maya Biosphere Reserve. Illegal logging destroys biodiversity, threatens indigenous communities, and accelerates climate change. The law protects forests and national parks.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment
exceptions: Licensed timber operations under approved forest management plans

quiz.q: Which region of Guatemala faces the most significant deforestation threats?
quiz.explanation: The Petén region, home to part of the Maya Biosphere Reserve, faces the most severe deforestation pressures in Guatemala.

laws.title: Gang Membership
laws.subtitle: Joining or operating with criminal street gangs
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala criminalizes membership in illegal gangs (maras) such as MS-13 and Barrio 18. These organizations are responsible for widespread extortion, murder, and trafficking. The law targets both membership and leadership of criminal gangs.
laws.penalty: 6 to 12 years imprisonment; enhanced for leaders
exceptions: None — knowing gang membership is criminal

quiz.q: Which gangs are most associated with criminal activity in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: MS-13 and Barrio 18 (18th Street Gang) are the dominant criminal street gangs operating in Guatemala.

laws.title: Child Labor
laws.subtitle: Employing children in prohibited work
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala sets the minimum working age at 14, with restrictions on the types of work children under 18 may perform. Child labor remains a serious problem, particularly in agriculture where children work on coffee and sugar plantations. Full-time school attendance is required for working minors.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 2 years imprisonment for employers
exceptions: Light family agricultural work with school attendance maintained

quiz.q: In which industry is child labor most prevalent in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Agricultural work on coffee and sugar plantations remains the most common form of child labor in Guatemala.

laws.title: Extortion
laws.subtitle: Demanding money through threats or violence
laws.fullDescription: Extortion by criminal gangs is one of Guatemala most serious crimes. Businesses, bus drivers, market vendors, and ordinary citizens are regularly subjected to extortion demands called renta (rent). Failing to pay can result in violence. The law treats extortion as a serious organized crime.
laws.penalty: 6 to 15 years imprisonment
exceptions: None — extortion is always criminal

quiz.q: What is the local term for gang extortion payments in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Extortion payments demanded by gangs in Guatemala are colloquially called renta (rent), implying regular mandatory payments.

laws.title: Water Source Contamination
laws.subtitle: Polluting rivers or groundwater sources
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala faces serious water pollution problems from agricultural runoff, mining operations, and inadequate sewage treatment. Contaminating water sources that communities depend on for drinking and agriculture is prohibited under environmental law.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 4 years imprisonment for industrial contamination
exceptions: Accidental spills with immediate reporting and remediation

quiz.q: What are the main causes of water contamination in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Agricultural runoff, mining operations, and inadequate sewage treatment are the primary sources of water contamination in Guatemala.

laws.title: Femicide
laws.subtitle: Killing a woman because of her gender
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala enacted a specific femicide law in 2008 following alarming rates of violence against women. The law criminalizes killing a woman in the context of gender-based power relations, including domestic violence, sexual violence, and other gendered contexts.
laws.penalty: 25 to 50 years imprisonment
exceptions: None — femicide carries no exceptions
laws.sourceLabel: Guatemala Law Against Femicide and Other Forms of Violence Against Women

quiz.q: When did Guatemala enact its specific femicide law?
quiz.explanation: Guatemala enacted its femicide law in 2008 in response to alarming rates of gender-based violence against women.

laws.title: Tax Evasion
laws.subtitle: Concealing income to avoid tax obligations
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala tax administration (SAT) enforces tax compliance on businesses and individuals. Deliberately concealing income, falsifying accounts, or using fraudulent schemes to avoid taxes is a criminal offense that undermines public revenue for education and infrastructure.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 6 years imprisonment for large-scale evasion
exceptions: Legitimate tax deductions within the law

quiz.q: What is the name of Guatemala tax administration agency?
quiz.explanation: SAT (Superintendencia de Administración Tributaria) is Guatemala tax administration authority responsible for enforcing tax compliance.

laws.title: Maya Archaeological Site Looting
laws.subtitle: Stealing or damaging ancient Maya ruins
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala is home to extraordinary Maya archaeological sites including Tikal, El Mirador, and Quiriguá. Looting artifacts from these protected sites or damaging ancient structures is a serious crime that destroys irreplaceable cultural heritage.
laws.penalty: 4 to 8 years imprisonment; mandatory restitution
exceptions: Licensed archaeological research with government permits

quiz.q: Which famous Maya archaeological site is located in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Tikal, one of the greatest Maya cities, is located in Guatemala Petén region and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

laws.title: Vehicle Theft
laws.subtitle: Stealing motor vehicles
laws.fullDescription: Vehicle theft is a significant problem in Guatemala, often linked to organized crime networks that strip vehicles or move them across borders. The law criminalizes theft of all motor vehicles and enhanced penalties apply when vehicles are used in other crimes.
laws.penalty: 4 to 8 years imprisonment
exceptions: None

quiz.q: How is stolen vehicle crime often connected to larger criminal networks in Guatemala?
options: Organized networks strip or export stolen vehicles
quiz.explanation: Organized criminal networks in Guatemala frequently steal vehicles to strip for parts or traffic across borders to neighboring countries.

laws.title: Counterfeit Medicine Sales
laws.subtitle: Selling fake or substandard pharmaceutical products
laws.fullDescription: The sale of counterfeit or substandard medicines is a serious public health threat in Guatemala. Unregulated markets and weak enforcement have allowed fake pharmaceuticals to circulate. The law requires all medicines to be registered and meet quality standards.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment
exceptions: Licensed pharmacies dispensing registered medicines

quiz.q: What makes counterfeit medicines particularly dangerous in Guatemala?
options: They may be ineffective or harmful and target vulnerable populations
quiz.explanation: Counterfeit medicines in Guatemala can be ineffective or actively harmful, particularly dangerous given limited healthcare access in rural communities.

laws.title: Child Sexual Abuse
laws.subtitle: Sexual exploitation or abuse of minors
laws.fullDescription: Guatemalan law strongly protects children from sexual abuse and exploitation. The law covers both contact offenses and the production and distribution of child sexual abuse material. Guatemala has strengthened these protections following concerns about exploitation of vulnerable children.
laws.penalty: 10 to 20 years imprisonment
exceptions: None
laws.sourceLabel: Guatemala Law Against Sexual Violence — Child Protection

quiz.q: What legislative framework primarily protects children from sexual abuse in Guatemala?
options: Law Against Sexual Violence, Exploitation and Trafficking
quiz.explanation: Guatemala Law Against Sexual Violence, Exploitation and Trafficking is the primary framework protecting children from sexual abuse.

laws.title: Illegal Mining Operations
laws.subtitle: Extracting minerals without permits
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala has significant mineral resources and contentious mining conflicts, particularly involving indigenous communities. Operating mines without proper environmental permits, or in areas where mining is prohibited, violates both environmental law and indigenous rights protections.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 6 years imprisonment
exceptions: Small-scale artisan mining under specific frameworks

quiz.q: What makes mining conflicts particularly complex in Guatemala?
options: Conflicts involving indigenous community rights and environmental concerns
quiz.explanation: Mining in Guatemala is particularly contentious because operations often affect indigenous community lands and water sources.

laws.title: Cybercrime and Online Fraud
laws.subtitle: Committing fraud or unauthorized access online
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala criminal law addresses cybercrime including unauthorized access to computer systems, online fraud, and identity theft. As internet use has grown, so has digital crime targeting individuals and businesses.
laws.penalty: 2 to 5 years imprisonment
exceptions: Authorized security testing

quiz.q: What type of cybercrime is most commonly prosecuted in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Online fraud and identity theft are the most commonly prosecuted cybercrimes in Guatemala as digital commerce has expanded.

laws.title: Workplace Safety Violations
laws.subtitle: Failing to provide safe working conditions
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala labor law requires employers to provide safe working conditions and comply with occupational health standards. Violations that expose workers to preventable hazards — particularly in agriculture, construction, and manufacturing — are subject to penalties.
laws.penalty: Fine; suspension of operations; criminal charges if deaths result
exceptions: Inherently hazardous work with full protective measures in place

quiz.q: Which sectors have the highest workplace safety risks in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Agriculture, construction, and manufacturing have the highest rates of workplace injuries and safety violations in Guatemala.

laws.title: Arson
laws.subtitle: Deliberately setting fire to property
laws.fullDescription: Deliberate arson is a serious criminal offense in Guatemala. Forest fires set deliberately to clear land for agriculture are a particular problem that destroys biodiversity and contributes to the deforestation crisis. Urban arson is also criminalized.
laws.penalty: 3 to 10 years imprisonment; up to 15 if people harmed
exceptions: Controlled burns on own agricultural land with municipal permission
laws.sourceLabel: Guatemala Criminal Code — Crimes Against Property

quiz.q: What agricultural practice involves deliberately setting fires in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Deliberately setting fires to clear forest land for agriculture is a common cause of intentional burning in Guatemala, contributing to deforestation.

laws.title: Murder
laws.subtitle: Unlawful intentional killing
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala has one of the highest murder rates in Latin America, driven largely by gang violence, organized crime, and femicide. The criminal code imposes severe penalties for intentional killing, with aggravating circumstances increasing sentences. Anti-gang enforcement is a priority.
laws.penalty: 25 to 50 years imprisonment
exceptions: Proportionate self-defense
Accidental death without negligence
laws.sourceLabel: Guatemala Criminal Code — Crimes Against Life

quiz.q: What is the primary driver of Guatemala high murder rate?
quiz.explanation: Gang violence and organized crime, particularly MS-13 and Barrio 18 activities, are the primary drivers of Guatemala high homicide rate.

laws.title: Kidnapping for Ransom
laws.subtitle: Abducting a person to extort money
laws.fullDescription: Kidnapping for ransom is a significant problem in Guatemala, affecting both wealthy Guatemalans and foreign nationals. Criminal networks operate sophisticated kidnapping operations. The law imposes severe penalties and Guatemala has specialized anti-kidnapping police units.
laws.penalty: 20 to 30 years imprisonment
exceptions: None

quiz.q: What specialized unit addresses kidnapping in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Guatemala has dedicated anti-kidnapping police units (DEIC) that specialize in investigating and resolving kidnapping cases.

laws.title: Money Laundering
laws.subtitle: Concealing criminal proceeds
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala has strengthened its anti-money laundering framework under pressure from the Financial Action Task Force. Drug trafficking proceeds and corruption money are frequently laundered through real estate, businesses, and the financial system.
laws.penalty: 6 to 13 years imprisonment; asset confiscation
exceptions: None for knowing participation

quiz.q: Through what means is money most commonly laundered in Guatemala?
options: Real estate, businesses, and the financial system
quiz.explanation: Real estate transactions, front businesses, and the formal financial system are the primary money laundering channels in Guatemala.

laws.title: Forced Eviction of Indigenous Communities
laws.subtitle: Illegally removing indigenous people from their lands
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala has a troubled history of forced displacement of indigenous Maya communities, particularly during the civil war. Current law prohibits forced eviction from ancestral lands without due process. Indigenous land rights are protected under both national and international law.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 6 years imprisonment for officials who order illegal evictions
exceptions: Court-ordered evictions following full due process

quiz.q: What historical event caused massive displacement of indigenous communities in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: The Guatemalan civil war from 1960 to 1996 caused massive forced displacement of indigenous Maya communities, particularly in the highlands.

laws.title: Wildlife Trafficking
laws.subtitle: Trading in protected animal species
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala is a biodiversity hotspot with jaguars, quetzals, howler monkeys, and hundreds of protected species. Trafficking in protected wildlife — alive or as products — violates environmental law and international treaties.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 4 years imprisonment
exceptions: Licensed zoos and research facilities

quiz.q: Which iconic bird is Guatemala national symbol and a protected species?
quiz.explanation: The resplendent quetzal is Guatemala national bird and symbol, featured on the flag and currency, and strictly protected from trafficking.

laws.title: Illegal Explosives Possession
laws.subtitle: Owning explosives without authorization
laws.fullDescription: Guatemalan law strictly controls civilian possession of explosives and detonating materials. Unauthorized possession is a serious crime given concerns about their use by criminal gangs and in attacks on security forces.
laws.penalty: 6 to 13 years imprisonment
exceptions: Licensed mining and demolition companies

quiz.q: Why are explosives laws particularly significant in Guatemala?
options: Criminal gangs have used explosives in attacks
quiz.explanation: Criminal gangs in Guatemala have used explosives in attacks on security forces and rivals, making strict explosive control a security priority.

laws.title: Unauthorized Public Demonstrations
laws.subtitle: Organizing protests without notification
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala constitutional law protects the right to demonstrate, but organizers must notify authorities in advance. Demonstrations that turn violent or block critical infrastructure can be dispersed. The right to protest has been exercised extensively by anti-corruption movements.
laws.penalty: Fine for organizers who do not notify; criminal charges if violence results
exceptions: Spontaneous gatherings in response to immediate events

quiz.q: What major political movement in Guatemala used demonstrations effectively?
quiz.explanation: The 2015 anti-corruption protests in Guatemala were massive demonstrations that led to the resignation of President Otto Perez Molina.

laws.title: Discrimination in Employment
laws.subtitle: Refusing to hire based on ethnicity or gender
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala labor law prohibits employment discrimination based on indigenous ethnicity, gender, age, disability, and other protected characteristics. Discrimination against the Maya and other indigenous groups in hiring and promotion is a significant concern.
laws.penalty: Fine; civil damages to affected workers
exceptions: Genuine occupational requirements

quiz.q: Which group faces the most significant employment discrimination in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Indigenous Maya communities face widespread employment discrimination in Guatemala, particularly in formal sector employment and professional advancement.

laws.title: Document Forgery
laws.subtitle: Creating or using falsified official documents
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala criminal law prohibits the forgery of official documents including identity documents, academic certificates, and legal instruments. Document fraud is used to facilitate other crimes including immigration fraud and corruption.
laws.penalty: 2 to 6 years imprisonment
exceptions: Theatrical props clearly not genuine

quiz.q: How is document forgery often used in Guatemala criminal networks?
options: To facilitate immigration fraud and corruption
quiz.explanation: Forged documents in Guatemala are frequently used to enable other crimes including immigration fraud, identity theft, and corruption schemes.

laws.title: Drug Cultivation
laws.subtitle: Growing coca or cannabis for trafficking
laws.fullDescription: While Guatemala is primarily a transit rather than production country, law enforcement has discovered cannabis and poppy cultivation operations. Growing controlled plants for drug production is a serious criminal offense.
laws.penalty: 6 to 15 years imprisonment
exceptions: Licensed research cultivation

quiz.q: What is Guatemala primary role in the drug trade compared to production?
options: Primarily transit country with some production
quiz.explanation: Guatemala is primarily a transit country for drug trafficking, though enforcement operations have also found cannabis and poppy cultivation.

laws.title: Unlicensed Financial Services
laws.subtitle: Providing banking without authorization
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala banking law requires deposit-taking institutions and lending organizations to obtain licenses from the Superintendence of Banks. Operating unlicensed financial services exposes consumers to risk and undermines financial system stability.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment for organizers
exceptions: Microfinance cooperatives under specific regulatory frameworks

quiz.q: Which body supervises banking operations in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Guatemala Superintendence of Banks (SIB) licenses and supervises all banking and financial service operations in the country.

laws.title: Sexual Violence
laws.subtitle: Rape and sexual assault
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala law criminalizes sexual violence including rape and assault. The Law Against Sexual Violence, Exploitation and Trafficking provides enhanced protections and specialized courts. Rates of sexual violence are high and many cases go unreported due to social stigma.
laws.penalty: 8 to 15 years imprisonment; up to 20 for aggravated cases
exceptions: None

quiz.q: What specialized legal mechanism addresses sexual violence in Guatemala?
options: Specialized courts under the Law Against Sexual Violence
quiz.explanation: Guatemala established specialized courts under its Law Against Sexual Violence to handle these cases with expertise and sensitivity.

laws.title: Illegal Pesticide Use
laws.subtitle: Using banned agricultural chemicals
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala agricultural sector uses significant quantities of pesticides, some of which are banned internationally. The Ministry of Agriculture regulates pesticide use and prohibits the application of certain chemicals that pose serious health and environmental risks.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment for commercial violations
exceptions: Approved pesticides used within manufacturer guidelines

quiz.q: Which ministry regulates pesticide use in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: The Guatemalan Ministry of Agriculture (MAGA) regulates which pesticides may be used and enforces bans on prohibited substances.

laws.title: Illegal Gambling
laws.subtitle: Running unlicensed gambling operations
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala requires gambling operations including casinos, lotteries, and sports betting to obtain licenses. Operating unlicensed gambling undermines consumer protection and enables money laundering through gambling fronts.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 2 years imprisonment for operators
exceptions: National lottery operated by the state

quiz.q: What concern makes illegal gambling particularly serious beyond consumer protection?
options: It can be used for money laundering
quiz.explanation: Illegal gambling operations are frequently used as fronts for money laundering proceeds from drug trafficking and other organized crime.

laws.title: Tobacco Sales to Minors
laws.subtitle: Selling cigarettes to persons under 18
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala prohibits the sale of tobacco products to minors under 18 years of age. Despite having lower tobacco control standards than some neighbors, the law protects young people from nicotine addiction and associated health risks.
laws.penalty: Fine for retailers; license suspension for repeat violations
exceptions: None — sales to minors are always prohibited

quiz.q: At what age may Guatemalans legally purchase tobacco products?
quiz.explanation: Guatemala sets the minimum age for tobacco purchases at 18 years, consistent with most Central American countries.

laws.title: Organized Crime
laws.subtitle: Participating in criminal organizations
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala criminalizes participation in organized criminal groups beyond individual criminal acts. This allows prosecution of criminal network members even when specific crimes are difficult to prove. Anti-organized crime measures target drug cartels, trafficking networks, and extortion rings.
laws.penalty: 6 to 12 years imprisonment for members; up to 15 for leaders
exceptions: None for knowing participation

quiz.q: What advantage does organized crime legislation provide prosecutors?
options: Allows prosecution based on network membership even without specific crime proof
quiz.explanation: Organized crime laws allow Guatemalan prosecutors to charge network members based on their participation even when proving specific criminal acts is difficult.

laws.title: Illegal Immigration Facilitation
laws.subtitle: Smuggling migrants across borders
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala is a major transit country for migrants from Honduras, El Salvador, and elsewhere heading to the United States. Organized smuggling networks charge migrants thousands of dollars. Facilitating illegal border crossing for profit is criminalized.
laws.penalty: 6 to 12 years imprisonment for organizers
exceptions: Humanitarian assistance to refugees not for profit

quiz.q: Which countries are primary sources of migrants transiting Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Honduras and El Salvador are the primary source countries for migrants who transit through Guatemala heading toward the United States.

laws.title: Vandalism of Public Property
laws.subtitle: Damaging government or community infrastructure
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala criminal law prohibits willful damage to public property including government buildings, infrastructure, monuments, and public spaces. Given limited public resources, damage to infrastructure causes disproportionate harm to communities.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment for significant damage
exceptions: Accidental damage without negligence

quiz.q: Why is vandalism of public property particularly harmful in Guatemala?
options: Limited public resources make repairs disproportionately costly
quiz.explanation: With limited public resources, damage to infrastructure in Guatemala has a disproportionately large impact on communities that depend on public facilities.

laws.title: Chemical Weapon Use
laws.subtitle: Using toxic substances as weapons
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala criminal law prohibits the use of chemical or toxic substances as weapons against people. This includes improvised chemical attacks as well as any use of recognized chemical warfare agents.
laws.penalty: 10 to 20 years imprisonment
exceptions: Law enforcement use of approved crowd control agents within guidelines

quiz.q: What distinguishes a criminal chemical attack from law enforcement crowd control?
options: Law enforcement using approved agents within guidelines
quiz.explanation: Law enforcement use of approved crowd control agents within regulatory guidelines is distinguished from criminal chemical attacks by authorization and regulation.

laws.title: Consumer Fraud
laws.subtitle: Deceiving buyers with false product claims
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala consumer protection law prohibits misleading advertising, false product claims, and deceptive commercial practices. The Consumer Protection Agency (DIACO) enforces standards and handles consumer complaints.
laws.penalty: Fine; business license suspension for repeat violations
exceptions: Recognized advertising puffery clearly not taken literally

quiz.q: What agency enforces consumer protection in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: DIACO (Directorate of Consumer Attention and Assistance) is Guatemala consumer protection agency responsible for enforcing consumer rights.

laws.title: Electoral Fraud
laws.subtitle: Manipulating votes or election results
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala Supreme Electoral Tribunal oversees elections and the criminal code prohibits vote buying, ballot stuffing, and other electoral fraud. Guatemala has experienced significant electoral integrity challenges, making enforcement a priority for democratic governance.
laws.penalty: 3 to 8 years imprisonment
exceptions: None — electoral fraud is always criminal

quiz.q: Which body oversees electoral integrity in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: The Supreme Electoral Tribunal (TSE) is Guatemala independent body responsible for organizing elections and ensuring electoral integrity.

laws.title: Illegal Construction on Protected Land
laws.subtitle: Building in conservation or indigenous areas
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala protects national parks, biosphere reserves, and indigenous community lands from unauthorized construction. Building in protected zones destroys ecosystems and violates community rights.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment; mandatory demolition
exceptions: State infrastructure projects with full environmental assessment
laws.sourceLabel: Guatemala Environmental Protection Act — Land Use

quiz.q: What types of land are protected from illegal construction in Guatemala?
options: National parks, biosphere reserves, and indigenous lands
quiz.explanation: Guatemala protects national parks, biosphere reserves, and indigenous community territories from unauthorized construction.

laws.title: Impersonating Government Officials
laws.subtitle: Pretending to be a police officer or official
laws.fullDescription: Impersonating law enforcement or other government officials to extort money or deceive citizens is a criminal offense in Guatemala. Criminal groups have used fake police checkpoints and official impersonation for robbery and extortion.
laws.penalty: 2 to 5 years imprisonment
exceptions: Theater, film, and clearly fictional portrayals

quiz.q: How have criminal groups in Guatemala misused official impersonation?
options: Fake police checkpoints for robbery and extortion
quiz.explanation: Criminal groups in Guatemala have set up fake police checkpoints where they impersonate officers to rob or extort motorists and travelers.

laws.title: Food Safety Violations
laws.subtitle: Selling contaminated or unsafe food products
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala food safety authority regulates food production and sale. Selling contaminated, adulterated, or improperly handled food poses serious public health risks, particularly in a country where foodborne illness is a significant cause of child mortality.
laws.penalty: Fine; business closure; up to 3 years if deaths result
exceptions: Traditional home-prepared foods within community settings

quiz.q: Why is food safety particularly critical for children in Guatemala?
options: Foodborne illness is a significant cause of child mortality
quiz.explanation: Foodborne illness is a leading cause of child mortality in Guatemala, making food safety enforcement a direct public health priority.

laws.title: Aggravated Robbery
laws.subtitle: Theft using weapons or violence
laws.fullDescription: Armed robbery is a serious and common crime in Guatemala. The law distinguishes between simple theft and aggravated robbery involving weapons or violence, imposing significantly higher penalties for the latter.
laws.penalty: 6 to 13 years imprisonment; up to 15 if victim injured
exceptions: None for robbery using weapons or force

quiz.q: What distinguishes aggravated robbery from simple theft under Guatemalan law?
quiz.explanation: Aggravated robbery in Guatemala is distinguished from theft by the use of weapons or physical violence, which significantly increases penalties.

laws.title: Illegal Waste Dumping
laws.subtitle: Disposing of waste outside authorized sites
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala faces serious solid waste management challenges, with widespread illegal dumping in ravines, rivers, and roadsides. This contaminates water sources and contributes to flooding. The law requires waste disposal in authorized sites.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 2 years for industrial waste dumping
exceptions: Emergency disposal with immediate cleanup

quiz.q: What environmental hazard does illegal dumping in ravines cause in Guatemala?
options: Water contamination and increased flooding risk
quiz.explanation: Illegal dumping in ravines in Guatemala contaminates water sources and blocks drainage, increasing flood risk during the rainy season.

laws.title: Intellectual Property Theft
laws.subtitle: Pirating software, music, or branded goods
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala intellectual property law protects software, music, film, and trademarks. Commercial piracy — selling counterfeit goods or unauthorized copies — is both a civil and criminal offense that harms creators and legitimate businesses.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 4 years imprisonment for commercial piracy
exceptions: Personal copies of legally owned content

quiz.q: What distinguishes criminal intellectual property theft from civil infringement in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Criminal IP theft in Guatemala involves commercial exploitation — selling counterfeit goods or unauthorized copies for profit.

laws.title: Terrorism
laws.subtitle: Acts of violence to intimidate the state or population
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala criminal code addresses terrorism, particularly relevant given the history of the civil war and ongoing organized crime. Acts of violence intended to intimidate the state, population, or international organizations are criminalized.
laws.penalty: 15 to 25 years imprisonment
exceptions: None — terrorism is always criminal

quiz.q: What historical context makes terrorism laws particularly significant in Guatemala?
options: Civil war history (1960-1996) and ongoing organized crime
quiz.explanation: The 36-year civil war (1960-1996) and continued organized crime activity give anti-terrorism laws particular historical and contemporary significance in Guatemala.

laws.title: Wage Theft
laws.subtitle: Failing to pay workers earned wages
laws.fullDescription: Wage theft — withholding earned wages, underpaying workers, or making illegal deductions — is prohibited under Guatemalan labor law. This is particularly common in the agricultural sector where migrant workers have limited recourse.
laws.penalty: Fine equal to unpaid wages plus penalties; up to 2 years imprisonment for systematic violations
exceptions: Legitimate payroll deductions for taxes and social security

quiz.q: In which sector is wage theft most common in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: The agricultural sector, where migrant and seasonal workers have limited recourse and awareness of rights, sees the highest rates of wage theft.

laws.title: Landlord Tenant Fraud
laws.subtitle: Fraudulent rental practices
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala law prohibits landlords from fraudulently collecting rent for properties they do not own, illegally evicting tenants, or making misrepresentations in rental agreements. Tenant protections are particularly important in urban areas with housing shortages.
laws.penalty: Fine; civil damages; up to 2 years imprisonment for serious fraud
exceptions: Legitimate evictions through proper legal process

quiz.q: What fraudulent rental practice most harms tenants in Guatemala?
options: Collecting rent for properties the landlord does not own
quiz.explanation: Collecting rent for properties the fraudster does not own or have authority to rent is one of the most harmful rental fraud practices in Guatemala.

laws.title: Piracy of Natural Resources
laws.subtitle: Illegal extraction of oil, gas, or minerals
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala has significant mineral and petroleum resources. Extracting these resources without proper concessions from the state — or bribing officials to obtain fraudulent concessions — is criminalized as resource theft.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 8 years imprisonment
exceptions: Small-scale artisan mining in designated areas

quiz.q: What natural resources are subject to illegal extraction in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Oil, gas, and mineral resources in Guatemala are frequently targets of illegal extraction or exploitation through fraudulent concessions.

laws.title: Telephone Scams
laws.subtitle: Fraudulent calls demanding money
laws.fullDescription: Telephone fraud — including fake kidnapping ransom calls, lottery scams, and impersonation fraud — is a significant problem in Guatemala. Criminal groups run organized phone fraud operations targeting both Guatemalans and the diaspora abroad.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 4 years imprisonment
exceptions: None — fraud is always criminal regardless of method

quiz.q: What telephone scam is particularly common in Guatemala?
options: Fake kidnapping ransom calls targeting families
quiz.explanation: Fake kidnapping ransom calls, where criminals claim to have abducted a family member and demand immediate payment, are a particularly prevalent phone scam in Guatemala.

laws.title: Illegal Volcanic Tourism Operations
laws.subtitle: Leading unauthorized tours to active volcanoes
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala is home to several active volcanoes including Volcan de Fuego and Santiaguito. Operating unauthorized tourist excursions to dangerous volcanic areas without safety plans and proper guides violates regulations and endangers lives.
laws.penalty: Fine; suspension of operations; criminal charges if deaths result
exceptions: Licensed tour operators with approved safety protocols

quiz.q: Which volcano in Guatemala is particularly active and dangerous for tourists?
quiz.explanation: Volcan de Fuego (Volcano of Fire) is one of the most active volcanoes in Guatemala and has caused multiple deadly eruptions, making unauthorized tours particularly dangerous.

laws.title: Attack on Security Forces
laws.subtitle: Assaulting police or military personnel
laws.fullDescription: Attacking law enforcement officers, military personnel, and other security forces is a serious criminal offense in Guatemala. Given the high rates of violence against police, enhanced penalties apply to attacks on officers in the line of duty.
laws.penalty: 8 to 15 years imprisonment
exceptions: Proportionate self-defense against unlawful police violence
laws.sourceLabel: Guatemala Criminal Code — Crimes Against Authorities

quiz.q: Why do attacks on security forces carry enhanced penalties in Guatemala?
options: High rates of violence against police make deterrence important
quiz.explanation: Guatemala has high rates of violence against law enforcement, making enhanced penalties for attacks on security forces an important deterrence measure.

laws.title: Securities Fraud
laws.subtitle: Misrepresenting investments to defraud investors
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala capital market law prohibits fraud in securities transactions, including misrepresenting investment risks, operating Ponzi schemes, and insider trading. The financial regulator oversees market integrity.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 6 years imprisonment
exceptions: Legitimate investment projections that prove inaccurate without intent to deceive

quiz.q: What type of investment fraud has affected Guatemalan investors?
quiz.explanation: Ponzi schemes targeting Guatemalan diaspora communities abroad and local investors have been a significant form of securities fraud in Guatemala.

laws.title: Racial and Ethnic Discrimination
laws.subtitle: Discriminating against indigenous people
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala law prohibits discrimination based on race, ethnicity, and indigenous identity. Despite the majority of the population being indigenous Maya, racial discrimination in services, employment, and public life remains a serious problem.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 2 years imprisonment; civil damages
exceptions: None — discrimination based on protected characteristics is always illegal

quiz.q: Despite having a majority indigenous population, what problem persists in Guatemala?
options: Racial discrimination against Maya people in services and employment
quiz.explanation: Despite the Maya being the majority population, racial discrimination against indigenous people in employment, services, and public life persists widely in Guatemala.

laws.title: Toxic Waste Dumping
laws.subtitle: Illegally disposing of industrial chemicals
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala environmental law prohibits industrial facilities from dumping toxic chemicals in rivers, lakes, or unsecured sites. Industrial contamination from agricultural processing plants and manufacturing facilities poses serious environmental and health risks.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 6 years imprisonment; mandatory remediation
exceptions: Approved disposal through licensed hazardous waste facilities
laws.sourceLabel: Guatemala Environmental Protection Act — Toxic Waste

quiz.q: What industries are most associated with toxic waste dumping in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Agricultural processing plants and manufacturing facilities are the primary sources of toxic waste dumping in Guatemala rivers and water sources.

laws.title: Illegal Hunting
laws.subtitle: Hunting protected species or out of season
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala wildlife law restricts hunting to permitted species during designated seasons. The country rich biodiversity includes protected mammals, birds, and reptiles. Hunting jaguars, quetzals, and other protected species is strictly forbidden.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment; confiscation of equipment
exceptions: Scientific research with proper permits

quiz.q: Which animal is most protected from illegal hunting in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: The jaguar is among the most protected animals in Guatemala, with its killing strictly prohibited and subject to serious criminal penalties.

laws.title: Obstruction of Justice
laws.subtitle: Interfering with investigations or court proceedings
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala criminal law prohibits obstructing police investigations and judicial proceedings. Witness intimidation is a particularly serious problem given gang control of communities where witnesses fear retaliation.
laws.penalty: Up to 5 years imprisonment; enhanced for organized intimidation
exceptions: Legitimate legal defense activities

quiz.q: What makes witness intimidation a particularly serious problem in Guatemala?
options: Gang control means witnesses fear violent retaliation
quiz.explanation: Gang control of many Guatemalan communities means witnesses to crimes face serious risk of violent retaliation, making witness intimidation a major obstruction of justice.

laws.title: Abuse of Public Office
laws.subtitle: Officials using their position for personal gain
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala criminal law prohibits public officials from using their position for personal enrichment, nepotism, or to benefit associates beyond their legal authority. This is distinct from bribery and covers the wider misuse of official powers.
laws.penalty: 2 to 6 years imprisonment; removal from office
exceptions: None — misuse of official position for private gain is always criminal

quiz.q: How does abuse of office differ from bribery in Guatemalan law?
options: Abuse of office covers misuse of position; bribery requires a specific payment
Abuse of office only applies to elected officials
quiz.explanation: Abuse of office covers using official position for private gain broadly, while bribery specifically requires a payment or benefit exchanged for official action.

laws.title: Cyberterrorism
laws.subtitle: Using technology to attack critical infrastructure
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala criminal law addresses cyberterrorism — using computer systems to attack critical infrastructure including power grids, water systems, and government networks. As digitalization increases, protecting critical systems from cyberattacks becomes a national security priority.
laws.penalty: 10 to 20 years imprisonment
exceptions: Authorized government security testing
laws.sourceLabel: Guatemala Criminal Code — Cybercrime and Terrorism

quiz.q: Why is cyberterrorism treated as a national security issue in Guatemala?
options: Critical infrastructure attacks can disable essential services for the population
quiz.explanation: Cyberattacks on critical infrastructure like power grids and water systems can disable essential services affecting the entire population, making it a national security threat.

laws.title: Illegal Aerial Surveillance
laws.subtitle: Using drones for unauthorized monitoring
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala aviation and privacy law restricts the use of drones for surveillance of individuals, military installations, and sensitive facilities. The rapid growth of drone technology has prompted regulations to prevent misuse by criminal organizations and invasion of privacy.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment; drone confiscation
exceptions: Licensed aerial photography with prior authorization
Official security operations

quiz.q: What concern prompted drone surveillance regulations in Guatemala?
options: Criminal organizations using drones and privacy invasions
quiz.explanation: The use of drones by criminal organizations for surveillance and the general invasion of privacy drove Guatemala to regulate aerial drone operations.

laws.title: Illegal Sale of Alcohol to Minors
laws.subtitle: Selling alcoholic beverages to persons under 18
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala prohibits the sale of alcohol to persons under 18 years of age. Alcohol is widely available and underage drinking is a social problem. The law targets vendors who knowingly sell to minors.
laws.penalty: Fine for vendors; temporary license suspension for repeat violations
exceptions: None — sales to minors are prohibited

quiz.q: At what age may Guatemalans legally purchase alcohol?
quiz.explanation: Guatemala sets the minimum age for alcohol purchase at 18 years, with penalties for vendors who sell to minors.

laws.title: Illegal Sweatshop Operations
laws.subtitle: Running factories with forced or exploitative labor
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala maquiladora sector has faced scrutiny over labor rights. Operating factories with forced labor, preventing workers from leaving, withholding wages, or violating labor standards constitutes serious criminal and labor code violations.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment for forced labor conditions; factory closure
exceptions: Legitimate factory operations meeting all labor standards

quiz.q: What is the term for export-oriented factories in Guatemala that have faced labor rights scrutiny?
quiz.explanation: Maquiladoras are export-oriented manufacturing facilities in Guatemala that have faced scrutiny over labor rights conditions and wage practices.

laws.title: Illegal Trade in Protected Plants
laws.subtitle: Selling or exporting protected botanical species
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala is a center of biodiversity with thousands of plant species, including many orchids and bromeliads that are protected. Trading in protected plants — particularly wild-collected specimens of rare species — violates environmental law.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment
exceptions: Licensed nurseries trading legally propagated specimens
laws.sourceLabel: Guatemala Wildlife and Plant Protection Act

quiz.q: What type of plant is particularly subject to illegal trade in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Wild orchids and bromeliads are among the most commonly trafficked protected plants in Guatemala due to high demand from collectors.

laws.title: Hit and Run
laws.subtitle: Fleeing the scene after causing a traffic accident
laws.fullDescription: Leaving the scene of a traffic accident without stopping to assist injured persons and report to authorities is a serious criminal offense in Guatemala. Given poor emergency services in rural areas, failure to assist can be life-threatening.
laws.penalty: 3 to 8 years imprisonment; enhanced if victims die
exceptions: None — duty to stop and assist is absolute
laws.sourceLabel: Guatemala Traffic Act — Duty to Stop

quiz.q: Why is hit and run particularly serious in rural Guatemala?
options: Poor emergency services mean failure to assist can be fatal
Rural accidents always involve property damage
Insurance requirements apply only in cities
quiz.explanation: Poor emergency services in rural Guatemala mean that failing to assist accident victims can directly result in preventable deaths from lack of timely medical care.

laws.title: Burglary
laws.subtitle: Breaking into property to steal
laws.fullDescription: Home and business burglary is common in Guatemala. Breaking and entering with intent to steal carries enhanced penalties compared to simple theft, reflecting the violation of security and privacy in addition to the property loss.
laws.penalty: 4 to 8 years imprisonment
exceptions: None for intentional breaking and entering

quiz.q: Why does burglary carry enhanced penalties compared to theft in Guatemala?
options: It violates security and privacy in addition to causing property loss
quiz.explanation: Burglary carries enhanced penalties because breaking into someone property violates their security and privacy beyond the simple property loss of theft.

laws.title: Religious Persecution
laws.subtitle: Attacking people based on their religion
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala constitution protects religious freedom. Persecuting, attacking, or discriminating against individuals or groups based on their religious beliefs is prohibited. This protection covers both the indigenous Maya spiritual practices and minority Christian denominations.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment; enhanced if violence
exceptions: None — religious persecution is always prohibited

quiz.q: Which religious practices are protected from persecution under Guatemalan law?
options: Both Maya spiritual practices and minority denominations
quiz.explanation: Guatemala protects both indigenous Maya spiritual practices and minority Christian denominations from persecution under its religious freedom provisions.

laws.title: Telecommunications Fraud
laws.subtitle: Fraudulent use of phone or internet services
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala telecommunications law prohibits the unauthorized use of communications networks, including SIM card fraud, unauthorized reselling of bandwidth, and interference with telecommunications infrastructure.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment
exceptions: Authorized telecommunications providers

quiz.q: What telecommunications fraud is particularly common in Guatemala?
options: SIM card fraud and unauthorized service reselling
quiz.explanation: SIM card fraud and unauthorized reselling of telecommunications bandwidth are among the most common telecom frauds in Guatemala.

laws.title: Occupation of Private Property
laws.subtitle: Illegally seizing land or buildings by force
laws.fullDescription: Land conflicts are a major source of violence in Guatemala, particularly involving indigenous communities, agricultural workers, and large landowners. Forcible seizure of private property — land invasions — is illegal, though disputes often involve competing claims to land with complex historical roots.
laws.penalty: 2 to 6 years imprisonment
exceptions: Court-authorized possession pending dispute resolution

quiz.q: What makes land conflicts particularly complex in Guatemala?
options: Competing claims with complex historical roots involving indigenous communities
quiz.explanation: Land conflicts in Guatemala are complex because they often involve competing claims between indigenous communities, agricultural workers, and large landowners with deep historical roots.

laws.title: Pyramid Scheme Fraud
laws.subtitle: Running investment schemes based on recruitment
laws.fullDescription: Investment fraud through pyramid and Ponzi schemes has affected many Guatemalans, particularly targeting remittance recipients and diaspora communities. The law prohibits schemes where returns depend on recruiting new investors rather than genuine business activity.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment for organizers
exceptions: None — pyramid schemes are always illegal

quiz.q: Which community has been particularly targeted by investment fraud in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Guatemalan remittance recipients and diaspora communities — who may have access to foreign savings — are frequently targeted by pyramid scheme operators.

laws.title: Assault on Human Rights Defenders
laws.subtitle: Attacking activists, journalists, or community leaders
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala has one of the highest rates of violence against human rights defenders in Latin America. Attacking journalists, indigenous activists, land rights defenders, and other advocates is criminalized, but impunity remains high.
laws.penalty: 10 to 20 years imprisonment; enhanced if the victim is killed
exceptions: None
laws.sourceLabel: Guatemala Criminal Code — Human Rights Defenders Protection

quiz.q: What does Guatemala high rate of attacks on human rights defenders indicate?
options: Significant impunity for violence against activists and advocates
quiz.explanation: The high rate of violence against human rights defenders in Guatemala reflects significant impunity for those who attack activists, journalists, and community leaders.

laws.title: Dam Construction Without Environmental Assessment
laws.subtitle: Building hydroelectric dams without required studies
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala has numerous hydroelectric projects, many opposed by indigenous communities whose lands and water sources are affected. Building dams without proper environmental and social impact assessments violates law and indigenous rights.
laws.penalty: Fine; project suspension; up to 5 years for responsible officials
exceptions: Emergency water infrastructure with expedited review

quiz.q: What groups most oppose hydroelectric dam construction in Guatemala?
options: Indigenous communities whose lands and water sources are affected
quiz.explanation: Indigenous communities in Guatemala are the primary opponents of hydroelectric dams, which flood their ancestral lands and disrupt the rivers they depend on.

laws.title: Forced Disappearance
laws.subtitle: Detaining a person and denying knowledge of their fate
laws.fullDescription: Forced disappearance — the arrest or detention of a person by state or non-state actors who then deny knowledge of the person fate — was widely practiced during the civil war. Guatemala law now criminalizes this practice following international human rights conventions.
laws.penalty: 20 to 40 years imprisonment
exceptions: None — forced disappearance is an absolute prohibition

quiz.q: What historical period made forced disappearance particularly significant in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: The Guatemalan civil war (1960-1996) saw systematic forced disappearances of thousands of civilians, leading to specific laws against the practice.

laws.title: Trafficking in Organs
laws.subtitle: Buying or selling human organs
laws.fullDescription: Guatemalan law prohibits commercial trade in human organs. Organ trafficking exploits vulnerable people in poverty. Guatemala has faced concerns about child organ trafficking linked to broader human trafficking networks.
laws.penalty: 8 to 15 years imprisonment
exceptions: Voluntary non-commercial organ donation

quiz.q: What vulnerability factor increases organ trafficking risk in Guatemala?
options: Poverty and desperation among vulnerable populations
quiz.explanation: Poverty and economic desperation make vulnerable Guatemalans targets for organ traffickers who exploit financial need to obtain organs for illicit markets.

laws.title: Unlawful Detention
laws.subtitle: Holding a person without legal authority
laws.fullDescription: Detaining a person without legal authority — whether by police officers exceeding their powers or private individuals — is prohibited under Guatemalan law. This includes informal detention by community groups engaged in vigilante justice.
laws.penalty: 3 to 6 years imprisonment; enhanced for public officials
exceptions: Citizen arrest when criminal caught in the act with immediate police notification
laws.sourceLabel: Guatemala Criminal Code — Crimes Against Freedom

quiz.q: What informal practice constitutes unlawful detention in Guatemalan communities?
quiz.explanation: Vigilante detention by community groups — detaining suspected criminals outside legal processes — constitutes unlawful detention even when motivated by crime prevention.

laws.title: Forced Labor in Agriculture
laws.subtitle: Compelling agricultural workers to work through debt bondage
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala history includes debt bondage forcing indigenous workers to labor on coffee and sugar plantations. Modern forced labor through debt manipulation, document confiscation, or threats is prohibited, though abuses continue in remote agricultural areas.
laws.penalty: 5 to 10 years imprisonment
exceptions: None — forced labor in any form is criminal

quiz.q: What historical form of forced labor affected indigenous Guatemalans on plantations?
options: Debt bondage forcing work on coffee and sugar plantations
quiz.explanation: Debt bondage on coffee and sugar plantations was a significant form of forced labor affecting indigenous Guatemalans historically, and modern forms of labor exploitation continue.

laws.title: Hate Speech Against Indigenous Peoples
laws.subtitle: Inciting hatred based on indigenous identity
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala law prohibits public incitement of hatred, discrimination, or violence against indigenous Maya and other native peoples. In a country where the indigenous population is the majority yet faces systematic discrimination, hate speech laws protect community dignity.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment; enhanced if violence results
exceptions: Academic analysis
Factual reporting on discrimination
laws.sourceLabel: Guatemala Law Against Discrimination — Hate Speech

quiz.q: Why do hate speech laws protecting indigenous peoples have special significance in Guatemala?
options: Indigenous people are a small minority
The indigenous majority faces systematic discrimination despite their numbers
Indigenous languages are legally equal to Spanish
quiz.explanation: Despite being the majority population, indigenous Maya Guatemalans face systematic discrimination, giving hate speech protections particular importance.

laws.title: Aggravated Homicide of Officials
laws.subtitle: Killing judges, prosecutors, or public officials
laws.fullDescription: Killing judges, prosecutors, witnesses, or other officials involved in criminal justice is treated as an especially serious form of murder in Guatemala. High-profile killings of anti-corruption officials have threatened the rule of law.
laws.penalty: 30 to 50 years imprisonment
exceptions: None

quiz.q: Why does killing justice officials carry especially severe penalties in Guatemala?
options: Such killings directly threaten the rule of law and undermine justice
quiz.explanation: Killing judges, prosecutors, and officials directly threatens the entire justice system and rule of law, justifying especially severe penalties in Guatemala.

laws.title: Disruption of Natural Disaster Prevention Systems
laws.subtitle: Damaging early warning or disaster prevention infrastructure
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala is highly vulnerable to natural disasters including volcanic eruptions, earthquakes, hurricanes, and landslides. Damaging early warning systems, weather monitoring stations, or other disaster prevention infrastructure endangers lives.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment; full restoration costs
exceptions: None — damage to disaster prevention systems is always serious

quiz.q: What natural disasters make Guatemala early warning systems critical?
options: Volcanic eruptions, earthquakes, hurricanes, and landslides
quiz.explanation: Guatemala faces multiple natural hazards including volcanic eruptions, earthquakes, hurricanes, and landslides, making early warning systems vital for community safety.

laws.title: Genocide and Crimes Against Humanity
laws.subtitle: Mass atrocities and systematic civilian attacks
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala criminal law incorporates international crimes following the devastating civil war in which the state conducted campaigns amounting to genocide against Maya communities. Prosecutions including the conviction of former President Rios Montt established accountability for historical crimes.
laws.penalty: 30 to 50 years imprisonment
exceptions: None — atrocity crimes have no legal justification

quiz.q: What landmark prosecution established accountability for genocide in Guatemala?
options: Trial of drug cartel leader El Chapo
Conviction of former President Rios Montt for genocide
CICIG prosecution of Otto Perez Molina
UN Tribunal ruling on civil war crimes
quiz.explanation: The 2013 conviction of former dictator Efrain Rios Montt for genocide against Maya Ixil communities was a landmark accountability prosecution in Guatemala.

laws.title: Domestic Violence
laws.subtitle: Physical or psychological abuse of family members
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala law criminalizes domestic violence through the Law Against Femicide and Other Forms of Violence Against Women. Physical, psychological, and economic violence within family relationships is prohibited, with specialized courts established to handle these cases.
laws.penalty: 5 to 8 years imprisonment for physical violence; enhanced for serious injury
exceptions: None for physical or psychological abuse
laws.sourceLabel: Guatemala Law Against Femicide — Domestic Violence

quiz.q: What specialized mechanism handles domestic violence cases in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Guatemala established specialized domestic violence courts under its anti-femicide framework to handle these cases with appropriate expertise and sensitivity.

laws.title: Illegal Street Vending
laws.subtitle: Selling goods in prohibited areas
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala municipalities regulate street vending to manage public spaces and commercial activity. Selling in prohibited zones, blocking pedestrian access, or vending without licenses in designated areas can result in fines and confiscation of goods.
laws.penalty: Fine; confiscation of goods; possible detention for repeat violations
exceptions: Licensed vendors in authorized market areas

quiz.q: Who regulates street vending in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Municipal governments in Guatemala are responsible for regulating where and how street vending may occur in their jurisdictions.

laws.title: Illegal Border Crossing into Mexico
laws.subtitle: Crossing the Guatemala-Mexico border illegally
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala borders Mexico and is a major transit point for migrants heading north. Crossing the border at unauthorized points is illegal for both Guatemalans and migrants transiting through. Organized criminal groups charge migrants for border crossing assistance.
laws.penalty: Fine; deportation for foreign nationals; criminal charges for organizers
exceptions: Asylum seekers presenting at official crossing points

quiz.q: What role do criminal organizations play in Guatemala illegal border crossing?
options: They charge migrants for crossing assistance as smugglers
quiz.explanation: Criminal organizations in Guatemala operate as smugglers (coyotes), charging migrants significant fees to assist illegal border crossings into Mexico.

laws.title: Unlicensed Broadcasting
laws.subtitle: Operating radio or TV without government authorization
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala requires radio and television broadcasters to obtain concessions from the telecommunications regulator. Operating unlicensed stations, particularly community radio in indigenous areas, has been a contentious issue involving free speech and spectrum management.
laws.penalty: Fine; equipment confiscation; up to 1 year imprisonment
exceptions: Community radio operating under specific limited licenses

quiz.q: What type of community broadcasting has been particularly controversial in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Indigenous community radio stations broadcasting in Maya languages have faced particular controversy over licensing, involving tensions between regulation and indigenous cultural rights.

laws.title: Sexual Slavery
laws.subtitle: Holding a person for forced sexual servitude
laws.fullDescription: Sexual slavery — holding a person and forcing them into commercial sexual exploitation — is one of the most serious crimes under Guatemalan law. This is addressed through the Law Against Sexual Violence, Exploitation and Trafficking and carries severe penalties.
laws.penalty: 15 to 20 years imprisonment
exceptions: None
laws.sourceLabel: Guatemala Law Against Sexual Violence, Exploitation and Trafficking

quiz.q: Which law primarily addresses sexual slavery in Guatemala?
options: Law Against Sexual Violence, Exploitation and Trafficking
quiz.explanation: The Law Against Sexual Violence, Exploitation and Trafficking is the primary legal framework addressing sexual slavery and exploitation in Guatemala.

laws.title: Vigilante Justice
laws.subtitle: Taking justice into own hands without legal authority
laws.fullDescription: Lynching and mob justice have resulted in deaths in Guatemala when communities take justice into their own hands. The law prohibits vigilante violence against suspected criminals, regardless of the underlying crime alleged. Community-based justice must operate within legal frameworks.
laws.penalty: 3 to 10 years imprisonment for participants; more for leaders
exceptions: None — lynching and vigilante violence are always criminal

quiz.q: What form of vigilante justice has resulted in deaths in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Mob lynchings of people suspected of crimes have occurred in Guatemala when communities felt official justice was absent or ineffective.

laws.title: Chemical Contamination of Food Supply
laws.subtitle: Introducing toxic substances into food products
laws.fullDescription: Deliberately contaminating food products with toxic or harmful substances is a serious criminal offense in Guatemala. This covers both targeted attacks and deliberate adulteration of commercial food products for economic gain.
laws.penalty: 10 to 20 years imprisonment; enhanced if deaths result
exceptions: None for deliberate food contamination
laws.sourceLabel: Guatemala Criminal Code — Food Safety Crimes

quiz.q: What motivates deliberate food contamination in commercial contexts?
options: Economic gain through fraud or harming competitors
quiz.explanation: Commercial food contamination is often motivated by economic fraud (adulterating to reduce costs) or sabotage of competitor products in Guatemala.

laws.title: Theft of Remittances
laws.subtitle: Stealing money transfers sent from abroad
laws.fullDescription: Remittances from Guatemalans abroad are a critical source of income for many families, representing over 15% of GDP. Stealing remittance payments at collection points, through fraud, or by intercepting transfers is a criminal offense with significant economic impact.
laws.penalty: 3 to 7 years imprisonment
exceptions: None
laws.sourceLabel: Guatemala Criminal Code — Theft and Fraud

quiz.q: Why are remittances economically critical in Guatemala?
options: They are a small fraction of income
Remittances represent over 15% of GDP and are vital for many families
quiz.explanation: Remittances from Guatemalans living abroad represent over 15% of the country GDP and are the primary income source for many families, making their theft particularly harmful.

laws.title: Medical Negligence Causing Death
laws.subtitle: Gross negligence by healthcare providers
laws.fullDescription: When medical professionals fail to meet accepted standards of care and patients die or suffer serious harm as a result, criminal negligence charges can apply in Guatemala. This is distinct from normal medical complications and requires serious departure from professional standards.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment; medical license revocation
exceptions: Acceptable complications despite proper care

quiz.q: What distinguishes criminal medical negligence from acceptable medical complications?
options: Serious departure from professional standards versus complications despite proper care
Whether the hospital is private or public
quiz.explanation: Criminal medical negligence requires a serious departure from professional standards, not merely an unfortunate outcome despite appropriate care.

laws.title: Corruption in the Judiciary
laws.subtitle: Bribery of judges to influence rulings
laws.fullDescription: Judicial corruption is a significant problem in Guatemala, undermining the justice system. Bribing judges, court officials, or prosecutors to influence case outcomes is criminalized. The CICIG commission exposed significant judicial corruption before its mandate ended.
laws.penalty: 8 to 15 years imprisonment; permanent removal from judiciary
exceptions: None

quiz.q: What anti-corruption body exposed significant judicial corruption in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: CICIG (International Commission Against Impunity in Guatemala) exposed significant judicial corruption before its mandate was not renewed in 2019.

laws.title: False Insurance Claims
laws.subtitle: Submitting fraudulent insurance claims
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala insurance law prohibits making false or exaggerated claims to insurance companies. Insurance fraud including staged accidents, false theft reports, and medical billing fraud increases premiums for all consumers and harms insurance system integrity.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment
exceptions: Good-faith claims with honest mistakes

quiz.q: How does insurance fraud harm consumers beyond the fraudster?
quiz.explanation: Insurance fraud increases costs for insurance companies, which pass these costs to all policyholders through higher premiums, harming honest consumers.

laws.title: Illegal Medical Experiments on Humans
laws.subtitle: Conducting unauthorized research on people
laws.fullDescription: Following the historical scandal of US-sponsored syphilis experiments on Guatemalans in the 1940s without consent, Guatemala has strict rules on human subjects research. All clinical trials require ethics committee approval and informed consent.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment if harm results
exceptions: Emergency compassionate use under expedited ethics review

quiz.q: What historical scandal strengthened Guatemala rules on human experimentation?
options: Nazi medical experiments affecting Guatemalan workers
1940s US-sponsored syphilis experiments on Guatemalans without consent
quiz.explanation: The revelation that US researchers conducted syphilis experiments on Guatemalan prisoners and mental patients without consent in the 1940s strengthened ethical research requirements.

laws.title: Unsafe Building Practices
laws.subtitle: Constructing buildings that violate safety codes
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala is highly seismically active. Buildings that violate structural safety codes endanger occupants during earthquakes and other disasters. Corrupt building inspectors who certify unsafe structures are also criminally liable.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment if buildings collapse; license revocation
exceptions: Minor non-structural deviations with disclosure

quiz.q: Why are building safety codes especially important in Guatemala?
options: Guatemala is highly seismically active with frequent earthquakes
quiz.explanation: Guatemala high seismic activity makes structural safety codes critical — inadequate construction significantly increases casualties when earthquakes occur.

laws.title: Impeding Emergency Services
laws.subtitle: Blocking ambulances or emergency responders
laws.fullDescription: Blocking emergency vehicles or preventing emergency responders from reaching people in need is a serious offense in Guatemala. Given limited emergency services, any delay can cost lives.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment if people harmed due to obstruction
exceptions: None for intentional obstruction

quiz.q: Why is blocking emergency services especially serious in Guatemala?
options: Limited emergency services mean any delay can be life-threatening
quiz.explanation: Guatemala limited emergency services coverage means any obstruction can critically delay life-saving response, making the offense particularly serious.

laws.title: Noise Ordinance Violations
laws.subtitle: Creating excessive noise in residential areas
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala municipalities prohibit excessive noise in residential areas during nighttime hours. Loud parties, commercial noise, and industrial operations that disturb residential peace are subject to fines and can be shut down.
laws.penalty: Fine; temporary closure of noisy establishments
exceptions: Licensed public events with prior authorization
Religious celebrations with traditional exemptions

quiz.q: Who enforces noise ordinances in Guatemala?
quiz.explanation: Noise ordinances in Guatemala are enforced by municipal governments, reflecting local responsibility for regulating quality of life in communities.

laws.title: Human Smuggling Networks
laws.subtitle: Operating organized networks that smuggle people
laws.fullDescription: Organized human smuggling networks that move migrants from Central America through Guatemala and Mexico toward the United States operate as sophisticated criminal enterprises. Guatemala law targets the organizers and financiers of such networks with serious criminal penalties.
laws.penalty: 8 to 15 years imprisonment for network leaders
exceptions: Humanitarian assistance to refugees not motivated by profit
laws.sourceLabel: Guatemala Law Against Human Trafficking and Smuggling

quiz.q: How do organized smuggling networks differ from individual smugglers?
options: They operate as sophisticated criminal enterprises with leadership structures
They only smuggle across one border
They are legal under international law
quiz.explanation: Organized smuggling networks are sophisticated criminal enterprises with financing, logistics, and leadership structures, warranting higher penalties than individual smugglers.

laws.title: Bank Fraud
laws.subtitle: Deceiving financial institutions for personal gain
laws.fullDescription: Bank fraud — including fraudulent loan applications, identity theft to open accounts, and check fraud — is a criminal offense under Guatemala banking law. Financial crimes undermine the stability of the banking system and harm honest borrowers and depositors.
laws.penalty: 3 to 8 years imprisonment
exceptions: Good-faith mistakes in financial applications

quiz.q: What is a common form of bank fraud in Guatemala?
options: Fraudulent loan applications with false information
quiz.explanation: Fraudulent loan applications using false identity, income, or collateral information are among the most common forms of bank fraud in Guatemala.

laws.title: Mass Deforestation for Agricultural Expansion
laws.subtitle: Clearing large tracts of forest illegally for cattle or crops
laws.fullDescription: Large-scale illegal deforestation for cattle ranching and palm oil cultivation is a major driver of forest loss in Guatemala, particularly in the Peten region. Companies and individuals who clear protected forest face serious criminal penalties beyond simple forestry violations.
laws.penalty: 5 to 10 years imprisonment; massive fines; restoration requirements
exceptions: Approved agricultural expansion on non-protected land with environmental assessment

quiz.q: What agricultural activities drive large-scale illegal deforestation in Guatemala?
options: Cattle ranching and palm oil cultivation
quiz.explanation: Cattle ranching and palm oil cultivation are the primary economic drivers of large-scale illegal deforestation in Guatemala Peten and other forested regions.

laws.title: Education Fraud
laws.subtitle: Operating fake schools or selling fraudulent degrees
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala education law requires schools and universities to be properly accredited. Operating fake educational institutions that collect tuition without providing real education, or selling fraudulent degrees, defrauds students and degrades education standards.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment; mandatory closure
exceptions: None — degree-granting requires accreditation

quiz.q: What regulatory requirement protects students from fake schools in Guatemala?
options: Schools require accreditation from the Ministry of Education
quiz.explanation: Accreditation by the Ministry of Education is required for schools and universities in Guatemala, protecting students from fake institutions.

laws.title: Crimes Against Peacekeepers
laws.subtitle: Attacking UN or international peacekeeping personnel
laws.fullDescription: Guatemala participates in international peacekeeping operations and has obligations under international law to protect UN and other international personnel. Attacking peacekeeping personnel is a serious international and domestic crime.
laws.penalty: Up to 20 years imprisonment
exceptions: None — attacks on peacekeepers are always criminal

quiz.q: What international obligation makes crimes against peacekeepers significant for Guatemala?
options: Guatemala is a permanent UN Security Council member
Guatemala participates in international peacekeeping and has obligations to protect such personnel
quiz.explanation: As a participant in international peacekeeping operations, Guatemala has obligations under international law to criminalize attacks on UN and international personnel.
